intendedFunction: A broad two-adult oak settle beside the main hall hearth, providing seating and a draught-screening back without obstructing circulation.
prompt: Author a cohesive two-seat late-medieval oak hearth settle with a broad horizontal silhouette, framed fielded-panel back, shaped arms, tapered posts, visible mortise-and-tenon construction, drawbore pegs, separately eased seat boards, and believable age. It must read immediately as shared seating rather than a high-backed chair.

cues.statement: The front view must read as shared seating with two occupant bays; width visibly dominates height.
A continuous structural frame contains separately inset fielded panels rather than disconnected vertical boards.
Rails terminate into posts with visible mortise-and-tenon and drawbore-peg cues; intersections cannot stand in for joints.
Two supported occupancy positions have an approachable seat and modest raked back.
Do not reproduce the narrow, vertically dominant silhouette of a single high-backed chair.

avoid: identical grain phase on adjacent boards
